note: Pool the builder draws one art direction from per video, skipping the ones in pipeline/history.json's last 5 entries. Each brief is a starting point: the palette still comes from the subject's own logos and artwork.

directions.name: Photocopied zine
directions.brief: Black-and-white photocopy texture, halftone dots, cut-out logos with rough paper edges, one spot colour from the subject's logo. Headlines set huge and tight, slightly rotated. Shots slam in like pages being slapped onto a desk.

directions.name: Pixel RPG quest
directions.brief: The video is a quest: each step is a level, options are characters with stat bars, the verdict is a boss fight or a treasure chest. Chunky pixel frames, stepped (not eased) motion, a pixel display face only for headlines.

directions.name: Engineer's notebook
directions.brief: Squared paper, hand-drawn boxes and arrows drawn on with stroke animation, sticky notes for asides, highlighter swipes on key words. Logos taped in. Feels like someone explaining on paper.

directions.name: Ops console
directions.brief: Dense monitoring dashboard: panels, live-looking counters, log lines scrolling, status lights. Comparisons as two services' health panels. Mono for data, a wide grotesk for headlines. Real commands typed in the terminal.

directions.name: Retro desktop OS
directions.brief: Windows 98 / classic Mac desktop: every fact is a window or dialog box that pops open, buttons, title bars, a progress bar for install steps, a fake error dialog as the hook.

directions.name: Sports broadcast
directions.brief: Head-to-head match: lower-thirds, scoreboard that updates per round, 'round 1/2/3' cards, a final score. Bold condensed type, team colours taken from each subject's logo.

directions.name: Transit map
directions.brief: The topic is a metro map: each option is a line in its logo colour, features are stations, the install is a route with stops. Thick rounded lines drawn on, clean sans, lots of white space.

directions.name: Shop receipt
directions.brief: Thermal receipt printing out line by line: features as items, costs and limits as prices, the verdict as the total. Mono type, torn edge, a barcode at the end. Paper on a dark counter.

directions.name: Magazine spread
directions.brief: Each shot is a magazine cover or spread: giant masthead-style headline, cover lines around a hero image of the logo, page numbers. Strong serif display with a plain sans for cover lines.

directions.name: VHS tape
directions.brief: Recorded-off-TV look: tracking lines and chroma bleed on edges, a PLAY or FF flash only on a cut. Chapters as tape counter jumps that sit in the shot, not a REC label or timestamp left on screen. Keep the text itself sharp and readable above the noise.

directions.name: Trading cards
directions.brief: Each option is a collectible card with art, type, and stats that flips to show its back; comparisons as two cards side by side with stats lighting up. Card frames tinted from each logo.

directions.name: Blueprint
directions.brief: Technical drawing: blue paper, white line work, dimension lines and callouts pointing at parts of a diagram of how the thing works. Lines draw on; labels in a narrow technical sans.

directions.name: Group chat
directions.brief: The whole video plays as a messaging thread: the question arrives as a message, answers as bubbles, logos as avatars, commands as code blocks someone pastes. Typing indicators between beats.

directions.name: Kinetic type
directions.brief: Almost no imagery: words are the visuals. Huge type that fills the frame, words swapping on the voice's beat, one word per beat at key moments, colour flips between shots. Logos appear only as punctuation.

directions.name: 3D product shots
directions.brief: Real 3D with the kit's Stage3D: each tool is an object on a turntable or a plinth (its avatar as a texture on a slab, a coin or a box), lit like a product photo against a deep backdrop in the logo's colour. The camera dollies and orbits slowly; cuts change the angle. Text stays flat HTML laid over the scene, set large and sparse.

directions.name: Server room flythrough
directions.brief: Real 3D with the kit's Stage3D: racks, blinking status lights and cables built from simple boxes and planes, low-key light with one coloured key light from the subject's logo. The camera glides down an aisle and stops on the rack that matters for each line. Commands appear on a flat terminal laid over the scene.

directions.name: Floating 3D diagram
directions.brief: Real 3D with the kit's Stage3D: the topic as a diagram floating in space, with tools as thick tiles carrying their avatars, connected by tubes or arcs, seen from a tilted isometric camera that swings to each part as the voice reaches it. Clean, bright, matte materials; flat HTML labels beside the tiles.

directions.name: Paper meme explainer
directions.brief: The Vietnamese TikTok explainer look: a full-frame photo of crumpled white paper as the only background (npm run image -- <slug> "crumpled white paper texture"), never a flat colour. Headlines in a heavy condensed display font with Vietnamese glyphs, ALL CAPS, filled light cyan or a colour from the subject's logo with a thick dark outline (-webkit-text-stroke with paint-order: stroke fill) and a hard offset shadow; a smaller black condensed caps line under them. Facts as label/value pairs: a small outlined coloured label (VIEW, GIÁ, RAM) over a big black value, stacked down one side. One or two meme stickers per scene (npm run image -- <slug> "<emotion or object>" --sticker): a cut-out with a thick white outline (stacked drop-shadow filters) and a soft shadow, slightly rotated, with a white speech bubble when it reacts; the sticker shows the feeling of the line (facepalm, shocked, thumbs up, money, laptop). Everything pops in with a quick overshoot scale and a small wiggle, text word by word on the voice; between scenes, kit zoomPunch or whip transitions, no slow fades.

directions.name: Meme skit
directions.brief: The Vietnamese TikTok meme look: one still photo as the whole background, showing where the line happens (an office, a bedroom at night, a server room; npm run image -- <slug> "<place>"), changed only when the place changes. One or two meme animals acting out the line in the lower half: animated stickers from npm run meme -- <slug> "cat dancing" (or vibing, shocked, crying, typing), played with the kit Meme, big, mirrored when they face each other; green-screen footage with the kit GreenScreen only when no meme fits. At the top a big caption telling the situation in plain spoken Vietnamese with the kit MemeCaption (yellow, black outline), centred, at most 3 lines, replaced line by line. No other graphics, cards or icons; between captions a quick kit zoomPunch or flash, never a slow fade.

directions.name: Quiz show
directions.brief: A TV quiz: the question on a big glowing panel, answer options as 2–4 chunky buttons (A/B/C/D) stacked in the middle, a huge 3-2-1 countdown with a ticking ring during the guess scene, then the right button lights green and the wrong ones dim and shake, with a confetti burst. Saturated studio colours (deep purple or blue with gold), bold rounded type; the explanation scenes stay in the same set.

directions.name: News desk
directions.brief: A tech news bulletin: a slim breaking-news bar with a ticker at the bottom, a big '1/3' story counter, each project introduced on a card with its logo, name and real star count, lower-thirds for facts. Each story sits on its own full-frame picture (the story page's share image, or footage or a photo of its subject), darkened and slowly zooming, never a flat colour. Clean broadcast look: navy and white with one red accent, a strong grotesk; quick wipes between stories.

directions.name: Terminal tutorial
directions.brief: The terminal is the whole screen: a large, readable terminal window with a step counter ('Bước 1/3') above it, each command typed at a human pace with a blinking cursor, then a short plausible output line taken only from the research (or a green check, never invented logs). The headline sits above in plain bold type. Dark editor theme with one accent colour from the tool's logo.

directions.name: Top 5 countdown
directions.brief: A ranking countdown: a giant rank number (#5 … #1) slams in for each entry and stays as a watermark-sized numeral behind it, the entry's logo card with name and real stars, and a progress rail of 5 dots on the side. Rising energy: each rank a step brighter, #1 gets a gold treatment and a short flash. Bold condensed type.

directions.name: Documentary
directions.brief: A short documentary: stock footage full frame, graded slightly desaturated with a soft vignette, lower-third captions in a serif, a small date and place stamp when the story gives one, slow push-ins on footage, and key numbers set huge on black between scenes. Calm, serious pacing; quick cuts only at the turning point.

directions.name: What-if simulation
directions.brief: A cinematic what-if simulation made in code, seen through the viewer's eyes: the world fills the whole frame and moves the whole time (the kit's SatelliteZoom over the place in facts.json `satellite` for a fall or flight, else footage or photos of what is happening). A live counter ticks with the story, like ALTITUDE 119,635 FT · 104 MPH: a small spaced label, big tabular numerals, the unit small beside it. One short line of serif italic subtitle per beat, centred low. Subtle camera shake that grows with speed, a vignette, and colour that shifts with the story (thin cold blue up high, warm haze lower, red when it goes wrong). No cards, panels or logos; credit the imagery small in a corner.

directions.name: Pastel 3D explainer
directions.brief: Load the edit-styles skill and follow its pastel-3d-explainer.md. Cream and peach ground with soft drifting blobs, soft clay-like 3D hero objects, the real UI in a dark window floating and tilting over it, data as red-to-green UI cards, one coloured keyword per caption line, springy entrances with slow parallax. Problem, proof, one feature per beat, CTA.

directions.name: Breakcore Swiss
directions.brief: Load the edit-styles skill and follow its breakcore-swiss.md. A white Swiss technical poster cut hard on a 150 BPM grid (24 frames a beat): hairlines drawing on, dotted grids, micro-text, a heavy grotesque key word that slams and mirrors, gradient cones and black spheres, footage regraded every beat with ribbon trails, 2-frame flash and smear inserts on the snare, a portal transition, a seamless loop. Facts still hold still for a second.

pacing: Fast cuts: a new shot or visual change at least every 1.5s.
Few long shots: 3–5 shots, each building up in place.
Chapters: a title card before each section, then quick shots inside it.
